source.name: World Population Prospects 2024: total population by sex, all scenarios
source.publisher: United Nations, Department of Economic and Social Affairs, Population Division
source.citation: United Nations, Department of Economic and Social Affairs, Population Division (2024). World Population Prospects 2024, Online Edition (interim update for Togo, 19 January 2026).

medium.label: UN forecast
medium.description: UN WPP 2024 medium scenario, the UN's central projection: the projection years of countries/{ISO3}.json series (population on 1 July; this file uses the UN's PopTotal and the series its TPopulation1July, which agree to within 1 person).
medium.unDefinition: Fertility, mortality and international migration all follow the medium assumption: "Based on the mean probabilistic projections for fertility and mortality, and median probabilistic projections for net migration."

constant.label: If birth rates stay the same
constant.description: UN WPP 2024 constant-fertility scenario: from 2024 to 2100 each country's fertility rate stays at its 2023 level (South Korea 0.72 births per woman), while mortality and international migration follow the medium scenario. A what-if that shows where today's birth rates lead, not a forecast.
constant.unDefinition: "As the name implies, under the constant-fertility scenario, fertility in all countries will remain constant at the level projected for 2024. Meanwhile, mortality and migration assumptions are the same as those in the medium fertility scenario." (table II.4: fertility "Constant as of 2024", mortality "Medium", international migration "Medium"). In the published data the constant level equals each country's 2023 estimate (true for all 237 countries and areas).

notes: places[ISO3].medium and .constant are arrays of people on 1 July; index = year - startYear; null = missing.

places[ISO3].estimate is the past both scenarios share: the UN's estimates of people on 1 July (TPopulation1July, as in countries/{ISO3}.json series) for estimateStartYear..startYear - 1; index = year - estimateStartYear; null = missing.
UN PopTotal (thousands, 3 decimals) x 1000, rounded to whole people.

WLD is the UN's world aggregate. The UN did not revise aggregates for the Togo interim update, so WLD still counts Togo's superseded figures (1.1 million more people in 2024, 2.7 million in 2100: under 0.03% of the world).

adjustments.method: UN constant-fertility population x (revised medium / original medium), year by year
adjustments.reason: The UN's interim update of 19 January 2026 revised this place's population (Togo: census counts had been adjusted for undercount twice) for the medium scenario only. Its fertility and mortality rates are unchanged, and the release note asks users to read the other scenarios "taking into consideration the adjustments made here to the medium projection", so the other scenarios are rescaled to the revised population level.
